title: POC scoping: security & benchmarks for pilot - ZenoTech
summary: POC scoping focused on security/compliance requirements for a pilot (SOC 2 / ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs), workload sizing and benchmark plan. Agreement to run a 2-week bench with synthetic traces and one internal customer dataset; Redwood to provide SOC2 pack, SSO SAML guide, and benchmark template. Action items and timelines agreed.
next_steps: Redwood: send SOC 2 report + ISO summary and security whitepaper
SE: share benchmark template and synthetic load harness (k6 script)
Customer: provide sample dataset and peak QPS patterns
Security sync with Maya and Lina to map SSO/SAML and RBAC
action_items: Samir Patel | Send SOC2 package, ISO summary, and pilot pricing options | 2025-02-18
Lina Gomez | Share benchmark harness and suggested configs (batching/quant) | 2025-02-20
Arjun Rao | Provide sample dataset snippet and 7-day traffic histograms | 2025-02-21
Maya Singh | Confirm required audit log retention window and SLA requirements | 2025-02-19
header:
Date: 2025-02-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (ZenoTech Head of Security), Arjun Rao (ZenoTech ML Platform), Helen Park (ZenoTech CTO), Carlos Mendes (ZenoTech Infra)
Recording ID: ff-20250214-zenotech-7c9a
Notes: POC scoping call; primary focus on security/compliance for pilot plus workload sizing and benchmarks
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 48 minutes. Quick intros — I m Samir, AE at Redwood. Lina is our SE who will lead the benchmarks.
[00:00:12] Maya: Hi, Maya here. Head of security at ZenoTech. We re tight on timelines, want pilot started by early March if possible.
[00:00:20] Arjun: Arjun, ML platform. I ll be hands-on for the bench and data.
[00:00:24] Helen: Helen — CTO, quick observer.
[00:00:28] Lina: Thanks. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria for the POC, get workload sizing, agree benchmark plan and timeline, and map security requirements (SOC 2 / ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs).
[00:00:40] Carlos: Also want to understand hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs — basically latency needs and any data residency constraints.
[00:00:48] Samir: Good point. For pilot we typically recommend hosted unless you need VPC / on-prem for compliance. But we can do a Redwood Dedicated pool for the POC if you want predictable latency.
[00:00:58] Maya: Our SOC 2 auditor requires us to see vendor SOC 2 Type 2 or equivalent and details on KMS, encryption at rest, key rotation. Do you have that?
[00:01:10] Samir: Yes, we ll send our SOC 2 package — the report and a security whitepaper. Also include our KMS integrations; note some wording is auto-gen so if any term is off we can clarify.
[00:01:20] Maya: Great. We also need SAML SSO for pilot access and ability to map roles to RBAC scopes (who can spin up endpoints, who can see logs).
[00:01:30] Lina: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC. For RBAC we can map IdP groups to Redwood roles (Admin, Dev, ReadOnly) — we ll share an SSO mapping guide.
[00:01:42] Arjun: On the workload side: peak QPS? average seq len? We re mostly short prompts, 40–80 tokens up to 512 rarely. Peak about 1200 requests/minute during spikes.
[00:01:56] Lina: Ok, 1200 rpm peak — that s 20 RPS. We ll propose two bench profiles: steady-state 10 RPS and spike test 25–30 RPS for 2 minutes. Also need token counts and batch sizing.
[00:02:10] Maya: For audit logs, retention policy: we need seven years for certain flows, but for the pilot we re fine with 90 days — but need assurances logs are immutable and tamper-evident.
[00:02:22] Samir: We have audit logging with append-only storage and can export logs to your SIEM via S3 or direct syslog. For immutability we can show write-once S3 bucket configs and hash chaining in logs — I ll include the tech detail in the pack.
[00:02:36] Helen: Are you able to run the inference in our VPC? For regulatory reasons some of our data cannot leave our cloud account.
[00:02:44] Lina: We offer Redwood Private which runs in a customer VPC. That can be part of pilot but adds setup time — typically 2-3 weeks to provision. For an earlier start we can do hosted with strict data controls and then move to Private if needed.
[00:02:58] Carlos: Any difference in performance between hosted and dedicated vs private?
[00:03:04] Lina: Performance is consistent; differences come from instance types and quantization choices. E.g., if you want 8-bit quant vs full fp16 it changes latency. For Dedicated we reserve GPUs so latency is more predictable.
[00:03:16] Samir: To tie back to success criteria — what equals success for you?
[00:03:20] Maya: Security: vendor SOC2 plus SAML, RBAC, audit logs satisfied. Functional: latency under 300ms p95 for our common prompts and correctness within X BLEU-style metric — we ll define exact tolerance. Cost: demonstrable cost per 1M tokens under threshold.
[00:03:36] Arjun: Also non-functional: ability to export model traces/k-v cache info for debugging, and visibility into token-level cost.
[00:03:44] Lina: We can provide token-level telemetry and KV cache snapshots for debugging. Some names might be slightly off in auto-export — e.g., 'K-V cash' in older logs but we ll scrub that.
[00:03:55] [00:04:00] Speaker 6: (crosstalk) —
[00:04:06] Samir: For benchmarks, we propose: 1) Synthetic load with k6 script for RPS profiles; 2) One internal dataset run (red team style) across 2-3 model variants (e.g., base open model, quantized, and a latency-optimized variant); 3) Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, token cost, and correctness metrics.
[00:04:28] Arjun: For the internal dataset — we can provide a sanitized slice (10k prompts) and a more realistic 200 prompt heavy-latency set.
[00:04:36] Lina: Perfect. Timeline: if you can give the data and traffic histograms by Feb 21 we can schedule bench runs the week of March 3. That fits your early-March start.
[00:04:48] Maya: Questions on encryption for data in transit and at rest — is customer-managed keys supported?
[00:04:54] Samir: Yes, for Private we support customer-managed KMS; for hosted we support envelope encryption with your KMS in many clouds — I ll include exact integrations.
[00:05:04] Maya: Do you retain prompts or outputs in logs by default? We need control over retention and ability to redact.
[00:05:10] Samir: By default we retain minimal telemetry for 30 days. For pilot we can configure longer retention and allow redaction hooks; we also support per-organization retention policies.
[00:05:20] Lina: Note: some debugging requires short-term retention of prompts; we can do redaction and masking to satisfy PII rules.
[00:05:28] Carlos: On the SLA side — if we hit latency SLO breaches during pilot, what is remediation?
[00:05:34] Samir: For pilot we provide playbook-level response and can spin dedicated capacity or change model variant. For Dedicated customers we offer SLA credits; for pilot we agree on response times.
[00:05:44] Helen: Security review — our legal will want to run a DPIA and vendor risk assessment; do you have a SOC2 questionnaire answered?
[00:05:52] Samir: Yes, we have a completed SIG/SOC2 questionnaire; will attach answers and the SOC2 Type 2 report. Also have ISO 27001 summary page.
[00:06:02] [00:06:10] Maya: What about penetration testing and vuln disclosure?
[00:06:14] Lina: We do annual pen-tests and have a vulnerability disclosure policy. We also provide CVE timelines and mitigation notes. I ll include the contact point.
[00:06:24] Samir: Let s walk the actual bench metrics we ll report: p50/p95/p99 latency per model variant, tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens, memory usage, GPU utilization, and error rates. Anything to add?
[00:06:36] Arjun: Add cold-start times and KV cache warmup behaviour — we care about steady-state after warmup.
[00:06:42] Lina: Yes, we ll include warmup scripts and note cold vs hot latencies. We also measure prefix cache hit rates.
[00:06:50] Maya: For RBAC mapping — we need to restrict access so only 2 people can spin up endpoints, but 10 people can query. Can you do role scoping at the project/environment level?
[00:06:58] Lina: Yes, project-level roles and attribute-based mapping from SAML groups. We ll share the mapping doc.
[00:07:06] Samir: Any competitors or prior solutions you used?
[00:07:10] Arjun: We tried a managed endpoint on one of the clouds — it was ok but costs ballooned and telemetry was poor. We re evaluating both Anthropic and OpenAI but cost/latency tradeoffs are key.
[00:07:20] Samir: Understood. On cost modeling we can produce a forecast for your traffic patterns — Lina will run a cost simulation based on the sample histograms.
[00:07:30] [00:07:38] Speaker 2: (brief pause)
[00:07:42] Lina: About data residency — if data must remain in your region we can pin model serving to region; for hosted we have region options in us-east and eu-west. Private deployments run in your account.
[00:07:56] Carlos: Ok. For benchmarks, do you need network egress limits? We sometimes throttle external traffic.
[00:08:04] Lina: Not necessary — bench harness runs from your network into Redwood endpoints, we can also run bench from our infra to measure end-to-end if you prefer.
[00:08:12] Maya: On authentication for API keys during pilot — we need rotated keys and audit trail when keys created/used.
[00:08:18] Samir: Keys are auditable; we log creation, use, and deletion with actor identity. We also support short-lived tokens via SAML.
[00:08:26] Arjun: Bench question: do you support batching on the client or do you rely on server-side continuous batching?
[00:08:32] Lina: Both. We support client-side batching and server continuous batching. We ll include recommended batch sizes for your token distributions. For short prompts batching may not help much.
[00:08:44] Samir: Ok, let s state measurable success criteria that we can sign off after pilot: 1) Security checklist completed (SOC2 doc, RBAC mapping, SSO configured), 2) Latency p95 under 300ms for the chosen model variant on spike profile, 3) Token cost under $X per 1M tokens (TBD after cost sim), 4) Bench reproducible and logs available to your infra team.
[00:09:08] Maya: That s acceptable, subject to legal review on data flows.
[00:09:12] Lina: Action on our side — I ll prepare the bench harness and a step-by-step runbook including SSO test plan.
[00:09:18] Samir: And I will send the SOC2 package, iso notes, KMS integrations and a draft pilot SOW.
[00:09:24] [00:09:30] Maya: One last thing — for audit logs, can we get streaming to our Splunk instance?
[00:09:36] Lina: Yes, we support log shipping to Splunk/Datadog/S3 with enforced TLS. We can provide sample parser configs.
[00:09:44] Carlos: Are there any telemetry costs for logs?
[00:09:48] Samir: Logs export is included for pilot; at scale we have tiered pricing for long retention exports.
[00:09:56] Arjun: Ok, timeline recap?
[00:10:00] Samir: Customer provides dataset and histograms by Feb 21; Redwood shares SOC2 and bench harness by Feb 18–20; schedule pilot run week of Mar 3. Security sync mid-Feb (Maya + Lina).
[00:10:14] Helen: Sounds good.
[00:10:16] Maya: Quick note: we will run a short internal legal questionnaire after we get SOC2.
[00:10:20] Samir: Understood. Any blockers?
[00:10:24] Arjun: None from infra side. We just need the harness and a little guidance on network config.
[00:10:30] Lina: I ll include a network checklist and sample firewall rules.
[00:10:34] Samir: Alright, thank you everyone. We ll follow up with the artifacts.
[00:10:38] [END OF RELEVANT TRANSCRIPT — remainder is quick clarifications and off-the-record scheduling].

Note: Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, and product names slightly garbled). Some speaker attribution may be generic in the export.
